title: An interrupted setup resumes from its journal and never deletes valid content
statement: Killing setup after its journal has begun leaves a journal naming the last completed phase and an exact resume command; running that command completes the remaining phases. Killing it during the dependency bootstrap, which runs before any journal exists, leaves consumer project state unchanged, and rerunning setup repeats the locked install safely. A failure in any agent phase leaves an already-initialised planning scaffold in place and reports partial setup rather than rolling it back.
notes: PASS 2026-09-23 on EVD-0138, measured by killing real children rather than by making one throw. Inside the bootstrap, which runs before any journal exists: the project is byte-identical afterwards, no `.pi` survives, and an ordinary rerun completes. After the journal opens: what the killed run left records the phase in flight as running — true only because that status is written before the work — and carries an exact resume command naming the project. THE ARGUMENTS ARE PARSED OUT OF THAT COMMAND, not typed beside it, so a command naming another project, omitting `--resume`, or missing altogether fails the control; running them completes the remaining phases and leaves no journal. A failure in an agent phase leaves the scaffold and reports partial setup. THE MEASUREMENT FOUND THREE DEFECTS IN THE LOCK, EACH BY THE CONTROL WRITTEN FOR THE ONE BEFORE IT, ALL NOW FIXED: a killed run's lockfile made every rerun wait out the two-minute stale window; clearing such a lock by reading it and then unlinking it lets two recoveries both acquire; and claiming it by rename first moves a lock that went live in between, leaving the name free for a waiter while it is put back — which four racing recoveries caught in CI on their first run. Removing somebody else's lock is now serialised behind a gate beside it, taken by the recovery path and by the waiter's stale break alike, with the judgement that acts made inside the gate; a gate whose holder died inside it is reclaimed by age and death together, and one just taken is left alone. Setup still refuses another machine's lock, an unreadable one, and a live one.
